papers.title: Shaping & Monitoring Models through their Internal Representations
papers.tldr: Mechanistic Shaping trains models to obey specs on which concepts they express and which they rely on, across vision, medical imaging, and language up to 32B. Shaped concepts usually stay monitorable with the right probe class; the paper catalogs three geometric ways models can dodge a monitor.
summary: Training objectives underspecify how a model should solve a task, so systems can drive loss down while relying on undesirable concepts (for example gender when screening a résumé). Interpretability usually diagnoses this after the fact rather than controlling it during training.

The authors propose Mechanistic Shaping: during training, models are constrained so that specified concepts are (or are not) expressed in outputs/representations and are (or are not) used for decisions. They evaluate across vision, medical imaging (including CheXpert), and language, scales up to 32B parameters, and paradigms including classification, SFT, DPO, and GRPO. Because shaping can itself change representations, they introduce a hierarchy of monitor classes and analyze three geometric circumvention mechanisms (concept drift, erasure from a layer, and nonlinear re-encoding via a product-code construction).

Across settings, Mechanistic Shaping substantially reduces targeted behaviors while preserving task performance. In the runs evaluated, shaped concepts largely remain monitorable: refitted linear probes recover the concept in most settings, and the original probe stays reliable when gradients do not flow through its score. Takeaway: interpretability tools can be training-time control knobs, not only post-hoc audits—useful if you want prototypes or concept directions that stay readable after alignment. Caveat: the authors note other circumvention mechanisms may appear at larger scales; code is at github.com/goodfire-ai/reliance.

papers.title: Phonological Knowledge of Chinese Characters in Language Models
papers.tldr: Across 17 LMs, PinyinBench plus probing and activation steering show initials/finals are usable for generation while tone is highly decodable but weakly steerable; DS-v4-flash falls from 90%+ to 72% when only tone differs.
summary: It is unclear how much phonological knowledge text-only and multimodal LMs store about Chinese characters, and whether that knowledge is causally usable. Tone is especially hard to isolate from segmental features.

The authors introduce PinyinBench (homophones, initials/finals/tones, polyphones) and study 17 LMs with behavioral tests, layer-wise probing, and activation steering. They also compare models with and without audio-bearing training.

A frontier model (DS-v4-flash) scores 90%+ on homophone judgment when characters share no phonological features, but only 72% when they differ only in tone. Probing finds tone highly decodable early with modest depth gains, while segmental features start weaker and improve more with depth; steering moves generation via segmental directions far more than tone. Audio training improves tone decodability without matching steering gains. Takeaway: high probe accuracy does not imply steerable features—pair probing with activation steering when auditing concept directions. Chinese-specific benchmark.

papers.title: Routes of Reasoning: Reading and Reshaping Test-Time Compute in MoE Models
papers.tldr: MoE router logits probe reasoning behaviors nearly as well as the residual stream; editing expert router scores at inference cuts generated tokens by a median 30.4% (up to 63.3%) across four models with ≤0.5 pp accuracy drop.
summary: Reasoning models overthink by verifying and re-deriving long after finding a correct answer, wasting test-time compute. Prior interventions mostly clip length rather than targeting specific reasoning behaviors.

The authors label sentence-level segments with six behaviors (planning, execution, restatement, fact, reflection, conclusion) and train linear probes on MoE router logits versus the residual stream. Experts tied to a behavior on one dataset predict the same behavior on others across six datasets and five domains. They then edit expert router scores at inference to curb overthinking.

Router probes match residual-stream probes with about half as many features. Across four models and four benchmarks, editing cuts generated tokens by a median 30.4% (up to 63.3%) while accuracy never drops more than 0.5 percentage points and often rises; the model tends to stop once solved rather than skipping needed steps. Takeaway: for steering-like control in MoEs, the router is a cheaper intervention surface than residual-stream vectors. Training-free and model-family-specific; not classical activation steering.

papers.title: Prior-data fitted networks for variable selection
papers.tldr: Two PFNs for Bayesian variable selection—CD-PFN for conditional dependence and PC-PFN for causal parents/children—estimate posterior inclusion probabilities without MCMC and often beat existing methods on semi-synthetic and real data.
summary: Prior-data fitted networks are strong at tabular prediction but little used for classical statistical tasks like variable selection. Bayesian variable selection usually needs posterior sampling or dataset-specific modeling.

The author builds CD-PFN to identify conditional dependencies and PC-PFN to identify parents and children in a causal graph. Both networks output posterior inclusion probabilities without drawing posterior samples or fitting a new model per dataset.

On semi-synthetic and real experiments, CD-PFN and PC-PFN often outperform existing methods. Takeaway: PFNs are not only TabPFN-style predictors—the same in-context amortisation idea can target PIPs and causal neighborhood recovery for tabular analysis. Open-source software is available; the abstract does not report specific AUC/F1 numbers.

papers.title: Task-Aware Bitrate Thresholds for Codec-Robust Ultrasound Segmentation
papers.source: arXiv eess.IV, accepted at IEEE VCIP
papers.tldr: On prostate ultrasound segmentation under H.264/HEVC/AV1 streaming, all three codecs keep mean Dice ≥ 0.84 down to about 0.07–0.20 bits per voxel; H.264 needs 82% more bitrate than AV1 for the same Dice and 104.7% more for the same HD95.
summary: Remote robot surgery and tele-ultrasound stream ultrasound under tight bandwidth, so lossy compression is unavoidable. Downstream consumers are increasingly machines, so codec choice should be judged by task accuracy rather than human perceptual quality.

The authors evaluate H.264/AVC, HEVC, and AV1 on prostate ultrasound segmentation, reporting Dice and HD95, and match codecs at a common SSIM operating point. For each codec they find the lowest bitrate that still preserves acceptable segmentation, reporting 5th-percentile Dice as well as the mean to expose worst-case drops.

All three codecs keep mean Dice ≥ 0.84 down to roughly 0.07–0.20 bits per voxel; below that AV1 degrades gradually while H.264 drops sharply. H.264 needs 82% more bitrate than AV1 for the same Dice and 104.7% more for the same HD95. Takeaway: for prostate US AI pipelines that may see compressed tele-ultrasound, measure Dice/HD95 under codec settings rather than SSIM alone, and prefer AV1 when bandwidth is scarce. Accepted at IEEE VCIP; single-task (segmentation) study.

papers.title: Encoding and Propagation of Grammatical Number in Large Language Models
papers.tldr: SAEs trained on Pythia-70M isolate plural-noun and plural-verb features whose interventions flip number agreement; singular counterparts are weaker, suggesting a privative number code, with similar patterns in Gemma-2-2b and Llama-3.1-8b.
summary: Sparse autoencoders map LLM hidden states into human-readable features, but using them to track a single grammatical phenomenon end-to-end remains methodologically hard. Small models still show strong grammatical competence, making them a useful testbed.

The authors train SAEs on Pythia-70M and locate features for plural nouns, plural matrix subjects, and generating plural verbs. They intervene by removing or adding these features on subject tokens and measure whether the model produces plural versus singular verbs (are/do/have vs is/does/has). They compare against corresponding singular features and replicate on Gemma-2-2b and Llama-3.1-8b.

Plural features causally flip agreement as expected; singular features are less effective for the same task, which the authors read as evidence for a privative English number representation. Results replicate on the larger models. Takeaway: for SAE circuit work, tracking how a feature propagates across tokens (not only local activation) is a reusable method; also expect asymmetries between positive and negative polarity features. Limitation: focuses on one grammatical phenomenon and reports no released SAE weights in the abstract.

papers.title: Don't Replace, Complement: A Detector-Agnostic Subspace Signal for Near-OOD Detection
papers.tldr: PLUS builds a per-class SAE subspace from the m most class-active neurons and adds a whitened Mahalanobis score that improves near-OOD AUROC in all 126 detector–backbone combinations at one fixed fusion weight.
summary: Post-hoc OOD detection works well on far-OOD but struggles on near-OOD, because near-OOD inputs still activate class-characteristic feature directions. A score tuned for one regime often hurts the other.

PLUS (Per-class Low-dimensional sUbspace Signal) selects the m most class-active neurons from a sparse autoencoder, orthonormalizes the decoder directions into a per-class subspace, and scores inputs by whitened squared Mahalanobis distance in the predicted class’s subspace. The signal is fused additively with any calibrated base detector at one global fixed weight estimated from ID validation only.

Across 18 detectors and all 126 detector–backbone combinations, adding z improves near-OOD AUROC; far-OOD is broadly maintained or improved, with only marginal drops when the base score is already near-optimal. Takeaway: SAE decoder directions can be reused as a detector-agnostic near-OOD complement rather than only for feature interpretation. Not a standalone SAE interpretability study; abstract gives no per-dataset AUROC numbers.

papers.title: ShapleyOG: Fast Adaptive Shapley Value Estimation with Odd Gaussian Processes
papers.tldr: ShapleyOG matches ShaplEIG’s adaptive Shapley accuracy while cutting surrogate overhead by up to three orders of magnitude by modeling only the odd component of the game under paired sampling.
summary: Exact Shapley values need exponentially many coalition evaluations, so they are estimated from limited queries. Adaptive selection (ShaplEIG) improves sample efficiency but repeatedly refits a GP surrogate and becomes costly.

ShapleyOG notes that Shapley values depend only on the odd component of the game. Under paired sampling, a GP on that component alone yields the same Shapley posterior and selection criterion from half as many observations. The method refits the surrogate on a sparse schedule, updates the selection criterion cheaply in between, and extends quadrature schemes to the Shapley prior covariance.

On diverse games, ShapleyOG matches ShaplEIG accuracy while reducing overhead by up to three orders of magnitude, beating strong non-adaptive estimators at equal wall-clock once a single evaluation takes about a tenth of a second and a few thousand evaluations suffice. Takeaway: for attribution budgets in interpretability pipelines, odd-component + paired sampling makes adaptive Shapley practical. Preprint under review; abstract does not name specific ML tasks beyond cooperative games.

papers.title: Simple Meta-Learning for HPO and CASH Using Performance Representations
papers.tldr: Representing AutoML configs by their past performance across tasks, then using Bayesian ridge regression, reaches tuned TabArena multi-model performance in about half the trials of dedicated meta-learning baselines without pre-training.
summary: Bayesian optimization for HPO/CASH often feeds surrogates explicit hyperparameter encodings that struggle in high-dimensional spaces. Meta-learning baselines add complexity and pre-training cost.

The authors represent each configuration by its historical performance across prior tasks and pair that vector with standard surrogates, focusing on iterative selection from a fixed candidate set. They also apply maximal marginal relevance as a posterior-free acquisition rule, and evaluate on TabArena.

On multi-model TabArena selection/optimisation, a performance representation with linear Bayesian ridge regression beats dedicated meta-learning baselines, matching tuned performance in roughly half the trials; for single-model HPO it is a competitive second. The method needs no pre-training or tuning and scales independently of search-space dimensionality. Takeaway: for tabular AutoML around TabArena/TabPFN-style stacks, a cheap performance-history embedding can replace heavier meta-learners. Scope is candidate selection, not a full AutoML system with ensembling/cost models.

papers.title: Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing
papers.tldr: VLA-Tug probes VLA latents for early failure detection, gaining up to 30% early-detection AUROC over the best learned baseline and up to 44% top-3 failure-mode accuracy on unseen tasks, enabling lightweight steering.
summary: Vision-language-action models fail under distribution shift in ways that can damage hardware or people, so deployment needs a timely, calibrated, informative, and edge-efficient runtime monitor. Existing monitors miss these requirements.

VLA-Tug is a lightweight probe over VLA latent layers. Supervision focuses on the pre-failure segment of trajectories; thresholds are calibrated to bound missed detections and false alarms jointly. The probe also predicts failure mode. Training uses two VLA backbones, 228 simulation tasks plus 8 real-world tasks.

Pre-failure supervision improves early failure detection at matched false-positive rates by up to 30% over the strongest learned baseline. Under shift to unseen tasks, miss/false-alarm bounds remain valid in up to 86% of runs versus ≤21% for baselines; top-3 failure-mode accuracy rises by up to 44% over a majority baseline at under 1 ms/step. Takeaway: calibrated latent probes can gate lightweight steering when a policy is about to fail—analogous to monitoring concept directions before intervening. Robotics-focused; dataset of 3,180 episodes released.
